podcast.title: Faked Death and Life in Cuba Theory
podcast.body: Many people believe that Tupac faked his own death and is currently living in Cuba under the name "Casanova The Dawn." "If Kurt is alive, he could be hanging out with Tupac. He's believed he faked his own death and is now living in Cuba under the name Casanova the dawn"

podcast.title: Increased Stardom in Death
podcast.body: Tupac (referred to as "Two Pock") was a big star when he was shot, but his fame and stature grew even larger in death. "And although two Pock and Big E were big stars when they were shot, they became even bigger stars in death."

podcast.body: Tupac was a central figure in the intense rivalry between East Coast and West Coast hip hop, famously against The Notorious B.I.G. "Esa terrible pelea entre la costa este o yo este de Notorious Vicky de TuPak."

podcast.body: A songwriter who wrote songs for Tupac was mentioned as having attempted a financial strategy similar to Bowie Bonds. "another songwriter who wrote songs for Rod Stewart and Tupac."

podcast.title: Videos for Branding
podcast.body: Tupac utilized his music videos not merely to sell a single or album, but as a strategic tool for branding. In the hip-hop world, videos became essential for conveying themes of money, status, luxury, and identity, thereby solidifying an artist's public image. "Tupac, Missy Elliott, and Dr. Dre used their videos as branding, not just to sell a single or a album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Future of the Music Video - Part 2

xref.title: Coachella Hologram Performance (2012)
xref.body: In 2012, a virtual Tupac Shakur made a striking appearance at Coachella during a set by Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg. Though marketed as a hologram, it was technically an advanced projection using Pepper's Ghost techniques, appearing "awfully lifelike" and marking a pivotal moment in the development of simulated live performances. "Then in 2012, a very dead two-pock Shakur showed up at Coachella during a set featuring Dr. Dre and Snoop Dog."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 1: (100-91)

xref.title: Tupac Shakur Hologram Performance (2012)
xref.body: Dr. Dre performed at Coachella in 2012, featuring a groundbreaking appearance by a virtual Tupac Shakur on stage alongside him and Snoop Dogg. Although billed as a hologram, the technology was a sophisticated version of Pepper's Ghost, creating a strikingly lifelike 3D image and marking a pivotal moment in the development of hologram performances. "Then in 2012, a very dead two-pock Shakur showed up at Coachella during a set featuring Dr. Dre and Snoop Dog."

xref.title: Attempted Bowie Bonds
xref.body: James Brown was one of several artists who attempted to replicate David Bowie's financial innovation, the Bowie Bonds, by securitizing his own music royalties. "Other artists tried the same thing. James Brown, the songwriting team of Holland Dozier Holland, the Isle of Brothers, Ashford and Simpson, even the guy who wrote songs like I Love Rock and Roll for Joan Jett, and another songwriter who wrote songs for Rod Stewart and Tupac."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Career with Digital Underground
xref.body: Before launching his successful solo career, Tupac Shakur gained experience in the music industry as a roadie, dancer, and backup singer for the group Digital Underground. This formative period helped him get his start in performing. "Tupac Shakur was a roadie, dancer and backup singer for Digital Underground and that got him started on his journey to a solo career."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

xref.title: Posthumous Impact and Legacy
xref.body: After his death, Kurt's image elevated him to the status of icons like Elvis, Buddy Holly, John Lennon, and Tupac, profoundly influencing rock, pop, and even hip-hop through his music, attitude, and image. "From that point on, Kurt was up there with Elvis, and Buddy Holly, and John Lennon, and Tupac."
